item.title: Prompting People
item.description:
📝 even the concept I was explaining - definition, descriptions, potential follow up questions and edge cases in that order. What’s funny is that this isn’t even intentional - it’s what I believe in my head is the more “efficient” way to express my thoughts and ideas than entirely separate, broken up conversations. It made me realize that while we’re training AI to be more human, the conversations might be training us to be more structured and honestly I’m not sure if this makes me a better communicator or just a better prompt engineer, but it’s a hard habit to break.
🔗 Read more: https://kuber.studio/blog/Reflections/Prompting-People

item.title: Arpanet standardized TCP/IP on this day in 1983
item.description:
📝 Before this momentous decision, networks would use a mix of incompatible protocols and proprietary vendor stacks. With TCP/IP, an internetworking (and thus ‘Internet’) protocol was born, connecting these networks with those beyond their initial confines. Beyond its internetworking power, TCP/IP was attractive across several other fronts.
🔗 Read more: https://www.tomshardware.com/networking/arpanet-standardized-tcp-ip-on-this-day-in-1983-43-year-old-standard-set-the-foundations-for-todays-internet
